minutes.headline: Board approved a 5% technology fee on permits and adopted the Complete Streets plan and FY19 goals.
minutes.summary: The Select Board held a long public hearing on a technology fee for permits to help pay for online permitting maintenance, with members debating who should bear the cost before voting for a partial fee. It adopted the Complete Streets prioritization plan, approved a liquor license transfer and a skatepark event license, adopted three board goals and the town manager's goals, and went into executive session on litigation and the DPW union agreement.

what_happened.line: The Select Board imposed a technology fee on all permits, set at about half the level that would cover the full annual cost of online permitting maintenance.
The Board adopted the Complete Streets prioritization plan as presented, which lets the town apply for construction funding each year.
The Board adopted three board goals for FY19 and accepted the town manager's goals as presented.
The Board approved a liquor license transfer and a one-day skatepark fundraiser entertainment license with the fee waived.
Three board appointments were postponed to next week, and the Board later went into executive session on litigation and the DPW union agreement.

why_it_matters: Permit applicants will pay a percentage surcharge on permit fees, while the rest of the online permitting maintenance cost stays in the general fund, which is mostly taxes.
Adopting the Complete Streets plan sets the project order for state construction grants, so road and sidewalk work in town will follow that list if funding is awarded.
